Exact estimate of the factor and the nowcast over stored parameter draws

Source: R/exact.R
mfbdfm_exact.Rd

Replaces the sampled factor and nowcast paths in a posterior average by exact conditional calculations at a set of the chain's retained parameter draws. The parameter draws still come from the chain, so this removes the simulation noise of the latent paths and not any error in the distribution of the parameters.

Usage

mfbdfm_exact(fit, n_draws = 100, paths = 20, seed = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'mfbdfm_exact'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

A fitted ind_dfm() model carrying its draws, the default. A fit made before this function existed holds no volatility paths and is refused.

n_draws

Whole number, how many parameter draws to use, evenly spaced along the chain. At most the 200 stored.

paths

Even whole number, simulated factor paths per parameter draw.

seed

Optional whole number, for reproducible simulated paths. The caller's random stream is restored afterwards.

x

An object from mfbdfm_exact().

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class "mfbdfm_exact", a list with factor, factor_var, index, nowcast and nowcast_var, on the scales and date axes of the same components of fit, and nowcast_between (the conditional means, one row per selected draw), nowcast_within (the conditional variances, same shape, which with nowcast_between give the nowcast's predictive density as a mixture of normals), mcse_nowcast, n_draws and paths.

Details

For each selected draw of the parameters and the volatility path, the latent data and the factor given the observations are jointly Gaussian with a sparse precision matrix. The nowcast is linear in them, so its conditional mean comes from one solve, with no simulation. The published factor is a nonlinear function of the standardised one, so its mean and variance use paths draws from that Gaussian, in antithetic pairs.

Total variances combine the two parts: Var = E[Var(. | parameters)] + Var(E[. | parameters]). The first is what a chain has to simulate and the second is what is left to estimate from parameter draws. mcse_nowcast is the Monte Carlo error of the nowcast from the second part alone, treating the selected draws as independent, which the even spacing along the chain makes roughly true for a chain that mixes.

Applies to ind_dfm() only. A fcast_dfm() fit identifies its factors after sampling, so its draws are not comparable before that step.

Takes about 1 to 2 seconds per selected draw on a 46-series weekly panel.

See also

ind_dfm(), mfbdfm_quality(), mfbdfm_contributions().

Other model functions: mfbdfm_contributions(), mfbdfm_diagnostics(), mfbdfm_draws, mfbdfm_news(), mfbdfm_quality()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(mfbdfm_example_data)
set.seed(1)
fit <- ind_dfm(mfbdfm_example_data, length_sample = 100, burn_in = 20)
